cards.text: The book of Hosea, from a prophet the word of the LORD came to (Hosea 1:1), has just warned Israel about their idols (Hosea 13:2-3). Now its last chapter calls out, "Return, O Israel, to the LORD your God…" Friend, after all that, the door is being held WIDE open.

cards.question: The call tells Israel why they need to come back to the LORD. What does it say happened to them?

answers.text: They stumbled because of their sin
They were scattered by their enemies
They were misled by their kings

cards.text: And this call doesn't just say come home. It tells Israel what to bring AND what to say, like a friend who writes your whole apology text and then hands you back the phone.

cards.question: Israel is told to bring their ___ and return to the LORD.

cards.text: Then come the words. Israel gets exactly what to say to the LORD, and it starts with their iniquity.

cards.question: In the words Israel is given to say, how much of their iniquity do they ask the LORD to take away?

cards.text: ALL of it, no "just the little stuff, Lord, I'll handle the rest." Next they ask Him to receive them graciously, so they can present the fruit of their lips.
Next, the words Israel is given name what they won't count on anymore. It's like finally taking a contact off speed dial.

cards.question: In the words Israel is given, which nation do they say will not save them?

cards.text: No more riding on horses, either. Then comes the big one, and I bet this one was the hardest to say out loud.

cards.question: In the words Israel is given, they say they will never again call the work of their own hands their gods.
The words Israel is given end with why they're turning to the LORD: in Him the ___ find compassion.

cards.text: That's what Israel is given to bring back. Now the LORD speaks, and I'm leaning in like a guy who just sent that apology text and is staring at the little typing dots.

cards.question: The LORD speaks about Israel turning away from Him. What does He say He'll do about it?
The LORD says He will love Israel only after they earn it.
The LORD says He will freely love Israel, because His ___ has turned away from them.

cards.text: Then the LORD's words fill up with PLANTS AND TREES. First, He picks a picture for what He'll be to Israel.

cards.question: In the LORD's picture of plants and trees, He says He will be like the ___ to Israel.
In the LORD's picture of plants and trees, Israel will wither like grass in the sun.

cards.text: Israel will blossom like the lily and take root like the cedars of Lebanon. Flowers on top AND roots underneath, friend.

Israel's splendor will be like the olive tree, and his fragrance like the cedars of Lebanon. Friend, after years in a junk drawer I smelled like dust and old receipts, and Israel's about to smell like CEDAR.
Then the LORD says, "They will return and dwell in his shade…" Friend, shade like that? Somebody's pulling up a chair.

cards.question: In the LORD's picture of plants and trees, they will dwell in Israel's shade and grow ___.

cards.text: They'll blossom like the vine, too, and Israel's renown will be like the wine of Lebanon. Friend, that's FAMOUS.
Then the LORD calls out to Ephraim, a tribe in Israel (Hosea 13:1): "O Ephraim, what have I to do anymore with idols?"

cards.question: The LORD says it is He who answers and watches over Ephraim.
The LORD says He is like a flourishing cypress. Where does He tell Ephraim his fruit comes from?

cards.text: The closing words speak to whoever is wise and whoever is discerning: understand these things and know them.

cards.question: The closing verse says the righteous walk in the LORD's ways. What does it say those ways are?

cards.text: But the rebellious stumble in them. Friend, that word from the very first call is back: STUMBLE.
